subject: Request: Temporary preservation of tenant logs for active investigation
messages:
From: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@everspringhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Everspring Legal <legal@everspringhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for active investigation

Hi Rishi,

We have an ongoing clinical data discrepancy investigation involving tenant everspring-prod-27. Our legal team is requesting a temporary preservation hold on request/response and audit logs for that tenant beyond the standard 90-day retention window while we complete forensics. The window requested is +180 days, scoped to the tenant and to the following resources: inference request logs, admin audit trail, and API access logs.

Can Redwood support a scoped, temporary preservation for that tenant without changing global retention policies? If so, what evidence/assurances can you provide that the preserved slice will be isolated, encrypted, and accessible only to authorized Everspring and Redwood security personnel? We also need an initial estimate of how long it would take to provide a scoped export if we decide we need copies for legal review.

We appreciate a quick confirmation so we can brief our counsel.

Thanks,
Olivia Hart
Security & Compliance Manager
Everspring Health
olivia.hart@everspringhealth.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: everspring_forensic_scope.pdf (pdf)  — short scope doc from Everspring
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@everspringhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for active investigation

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear scope. We can support tenant-scoped preservation without changing Redwood's global retention settings, but we'll need to align on three items quickly: 1) exact log types and retention start date, 2) access control (who at Everspring will have retrieval rights), and 3) whether you want a Redwood-hosted hold (data remains in production but marked preserved) or an export snapshot to a signed S3/secure bucket.

Initial answers:
- Isolation: we can create a preservation tag on the tenant's log stream and apply access ACLs so only a designated security group can access it.
- Encryption: logs will remain encrypted with customer-specific keys; if you require a separate export we can wrap with a transient envelope key.
- Timeline: for a scoped preservation (tag + ACL) we can complete within 48 business hours once approvals are in place. For an export snapshot and transfer it would be ~3-5 business days depending on export size.

I've looped in Grace from Platform Security to confirm minimum evidence/data exports and Mina from Trust to handle any formal attestation you need.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Fw: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for active investigation — scope + action items

Grace / Mina — forwarding Everspring's request. High level asks are: +180d preservation for tenant everspring-prod-27, limited to inference request logs, admin audit trail, and API access logs. Olivia asked for isolation, encryption assurances, and a rough export timeline.

Proposed approach:
- Step 1 (48h): Apply a preservation tag to the tenant's log streams and create a restricted ACL group (redwood-sec + everspring-legal) with read-only access. No change to default retention config.
- Step 2 (48–72h): Run a scoped export job to an SR-encrypted bucket (signed URL) if Everspring requests a copy. Produce an export manifest and SHA256 digest.
- Step 3 (as needed): Provide a signed attestation letter (Trust) detailing the preservation actions, access list, and retention end date.

Questions:
- Grace: can you confirm we can enforce a tenant-scoped preservation tag via existing logging pipeline without introducing cross-tenant exposure?
- Mina: I'll need a short attestation template and suggested wording for the preservation letter (legal will want explicit dates and personnel).

If this is feasible we'll propose the two options to the customer (hosted hold vs export) and log the work in SEC-1723. I can own communications.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for active investigation — scope + action items

Rishi / Mina — quick update from Platform Security after initial review:
- Tenant tagging is supported by the log pipeline; tags are enforced at the ingestion layer and will not surface cross-tenant data. We will run an ACL validation before turning the tag write on.
- Preservation will keep logs in the hot store but mark them as non-expirable for the defined window. Cost impact: expect ~12–18% incremental storage for the tenant depending on query patterns. I'll confirm a size estimate after we run a retention slice sample.
- For export, we support delivering to a customer-managed S3 with server-side encryption; export job will provide a manifest and checksum.

Action items I will take: run a 48-hour retention slice sample (outputs: estimated size, sample manifest) and validate ACL enforcement. I'll attach the sample CSV when ready.

Grace O'Connor
Principal Security Engineer, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
